# Rise and Battle the Day

## Scripture
"Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong." – 1 Corinthians 16:13

## Reflection
Paul's charge to the Corinthian church was not a suggestion—it was a battle cry. Notice the sequence: be watchful, stand firm, act like men, be strong. Strength is not the starting point; vigilance is. Before a man can stand, he must first see clearly. The enemy rarely attacks head-on. He waits for the man who is distracted, tired, and spiritually asleep. Your alarm clock is not your enemy—your complacency is. Every morning you choose whether to drift into the day or to arm yourself for it. Faith is not passive; it is a posture of readiness. Strength in Scripture is never mere muscle—it is conviction held under pressure. It's the father who leads when he's exhausted, the husband who serves when he's unnoticed, the worker who keeps his integrity when no one is watching. Today, don't wait for motivation. Take your stand. The battle is already underway whether you feel it or not.

## Daily Challenge
Before your first meal, do 30 pushups. On each rep, say one word of 1 Corinthians 16:13 out loud. Let your body and your spirit rise together.
